title: A whole media center from one compose file

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Picture a home server that finds a show, downloads it, names it neatly, grabs subtitles, and serves it on your TV, all without you touching a file. That's MediaBoxDockerCompose.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's a lot of moving parts for one box.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is, and Docker Compose keeps them together. Everything hangs off one folder called ROOT, and every container shares the same user, group and time zone settings. Downloads land in one place, finished libraries in another, and each app keeps its own settings in its own folder.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So who does the actual finding?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Arr apps, the stars of the stack. Sonarr handles TV, Radarr movies, Lidarr music and Readarr books. They watch for what you want, ask indexer tools like Prowlarr or Jackett for a matching release, and hand it to a download client such as Deluge for torrents or NZBGet for Usenet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Arr app imports the finished file into the library with a clean name. Bazarr adds subtitles, Tdarr can transcode files in batches, and Plex or Jellyfin simply read the library and stream it. Tautulli shows Plex stats.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do the people in the house ask for things?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Through request portals. Ombi works for Plex users, and Jellyseerr for Jellyfin users. Plus Netdata for live host metrics, and Dashmachine as a start page linking to every app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is there more than the main file?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Optional stacks start separately. Samba shares the library on the network, a WireGuard server gives VPN access with a web interface, Portainer manages containers, and a Caddy file puts each service on its own address.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep downloads and libraries on the same filesystem, so the Arr apps can move files instead of copying them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine's companion repo, another-install-script, gives a menu-driven installer. It can set up Docker, then add containers one at a time from a list of 92, and open the matching firewall ports.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the quick start is just clone, edit the settings, and run docker compose up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's it. The page has the full diagram and a service table.
